criteria.reason: Merged record in a fixture repo: the ref holds shipped.json with "detached": true and the cursor at step 4 (past the merge step 3); ls of <common>/ensemble/ship fails with no such file or directory.
After merged, status prints recordPath refs/ensemble/records/f:shipped.json; the ref record carries recordRef refs/ensemble/records/f; no ship folder exists.
Over steps 4-6 the ref commit count rose with every save (next and record, 3 to 9) and the ref record ends status done, shipped true; no ship folder was ever created.

At the detach the tracked anchor was written to the ref custody.json stamped with the run startedAt; no ship folder or startedAt.custody.json exists; a later custody reconcile moved the ref anchor (moves entry added, savedAt updated) while the tracked copy stayed on the old anchor.
Local ref and git ls-remote origin show the same commit (5779dbf...); the bare origin holds the detached shipped.json.
With .git/refs/ensemble blocked by a file, the merged record reports recordRefError and writes <startedAt>.json plus current.json under <common>/ensemble/ship/f; no ref was created.
After start only: <common>/ensemble/ship and <common>/ensemble do not exist; only the tracked shipped.json is written.
Same run in both places: with the ref copy newer status reads the ref (cursor 4, recordPath on the ref); with the tracked copy made newer it reads the tracked file (cursor 2).

Control with a matching ref copy and later updatedAt reads the ref (cursor 6). Ref copies with a different startedAt, detached false, or a work identity that does not match the record.json are ignored: status reads the tracked file (cursor 3) in all three.
No tracked shipped.json: with the ref newer status reads the ref (cursor 4); with the pointer-named folder record newer it reads the folder (cursor 6).

A run produced by the pre-change code (commit f3be76d9) with nothing on the ref and no tracked file: status loads the folder record at cursor 4, start --resume returns resumed true, and next hands out step 4.

record of step 4 on the resumed legacy run wrote refs/ensemble/records/f with the legacy startedAt and the cursor advanced to 5 (recordPath on the ref). The ref first appeared at the next save that preceded the record.

Ref anchor (stamped with the run) differs from the tracked anchor; check --link merge with the PR head at the ref anchor exits ok true; with the PR head at the tracked anchor it fails. The gh call is answered by a throwaway stub.
Same fixture: check --link deploy with the identity output naming the ref anchor passes; naming the tracked anchor fails.

Ref custody.json stamped with another run: with the detached folder file present the anchor is the folder file commit and a check at that head passes; with it removed the anchor is the tracked commit and a check at that head passes; the other-run ref anchor fails.

Plain start on a checkout with no state folder restored closed.json from the ref, dropped the stale stamped custody, and custody reconcile --set-only returned anchor X (audited) while HEAD was a later commit. The stale stamped anchor on the ref was not used.
The ref held a detached shipped.json (startedAt 13:03:47); after the plain start the tracked shipped.json has a new startedAt (13:03:49) at step 1 and status reads it.
